explain.say: In Jane Eyre, a woman is locked in the attic of Thornfield Hall, and the house hides her like a secret. In 1979 two critics asked why. Feminist criticism asks how books show women, who gets to write, and whose voices vanish. The timeline shows how the questions grew.

explain.say: Look at the first two dates. In 1792 Mary Wollstonecraft argued women only seem weaker because they are denied education. In 1929 Virginia Woolf said a woman needs money and a room of her own to write, and imagined Shakespeare's gifted sister, who never got the chance. What stops people writing today?

explain.say: Two feminist readings of the attic. On the left, Gilbert and Gubar: Bertha is Jane's dark double, acting out the rage Jane must hide. On the right, Jean Rhys and Gayatri Spivak: Bertha is a Creole wife from the Caribbean whose story is silenced so Jane can rise. Which reading convinces you?

explain.say: Last stop: 1989, when Kimberle Crenshaw named intersectionality, how race, class and gender combine. Feminist criticism now reads them together. Wonderful. Challenge: in one chapter of any novel, count who speaks and who is spoken about.

faq.q: What does feminist literary criticism do?
faq.a: It studies how literature represents women and gender, recovers women writers, and asks how power, voice and silence work in texts and in literary history.
Elaine Showalter's term for criticism that studies women as writers, their history, themes and traditions, rather than only women as images in men's books.

faq.q: Who is the madwoman in the attic?
faq.a: Bertha Mason, Rochester's first wife, hidden at Thornfield in Charlotte Bronte's Jane Eyre of 1847. Gilbert and Gubar used her for the title of their 1979 study.

faq.q: What did Woolf argue in A Room of One’s Own?
faq.a: That women need money and private space to write, and that history denied them both. She imagined Shakespeare's sister Judith, equally gifted but given no chance.
asks: A Room of One's Own summary

faq.q: What is intersectionality in literary criticism?
faq.a: Reading gender together with race, class, sexuality and other identities, since they combine to shape experience. Kimberle Crenshaw coined the term in 1989.
asks: What does intersectional feminism mean in literature?

facts: Mary Wollstonecraft published A Vindication of the Rights of Woman in 1792.
Gilbert and Gubar's The Madwoman in the Attic was published in 1979.
Jean Rhys's Wide Sargasso Sea (1966) tells Bertha's story before Jane Eyre.
